title: How far a learner may seek ahead
statement: Whether a narrated lesson should let learners seek forward only through narration already heard, or anywhere short of the next unanswered check, is untested.
detail: The narration handoff for one build of a narrated opening let the learner pause, seek within heard audio and replay, and real-browser QA measured it: a seek to 40 s with 29.68 s heard landed at 30.25 s, and the slider's maximum equalled the time heard. The handover's acceptance list asked that seek restrictions match the heard-audio design without making replay impossible. The film player tested the same day stops a seek only at an unanswered check instead: after the first check, a seek to 120 s was allowed and a seek to 190 s was clamped to 172 s, the second check. Nothing has compared the two designs with learners.
against: A testing limit, not a counter: "under `python3 -m http.server`, which does not honour Range requests, Chrome cannot seek inside the AAC clips: rewind and seek reset `currentTime` to 0." (g9/prototypes/app-narrated-qa/QA.md, line 7), so a seek test needs a server that supports range requests.

evidence.quote: The learner can pause, seek within heard audio, and replay.
Seek limited to heard audio | PASS | tried 40 s with 29.68 s heard → landed 30.25 s; slider max = heard (30.18)
Seek restrictions match the intended heard-audio behavior and do not make replay impossible.
Scrubbing cannot pass an unanswered check.
After check 1 done: seek to 120 s allowed; seek to 190 s clamped to 172 s (check 2)
